## What exists (high level; details in `01-architecture.md`)

Config and profiles; IDs, events, ledger; headless run wrapper; preflight and 3-source kill switch; guard hooks and role tool lists; state branch; Notion layer (bootstrap, map, mirror, outbox, value-based conflicts); `init`, `status`, `pause`; orchestrator agent v0; 58-artifact catalog with 28 draft templates; live test tier; four judge reviews in `docs/process/reviews/`.

Not built: everything in Stages 1 to 5, including the eight other agents, the state machine, dispatcher, merge/publish scripts, digest, cost, gates, meetings, sandbox.

## Orientation

If you are new: `CONCEPT.md` first. ARIMA is a replica of a company software team (roles, gated phases, 58 owned artifacts, scheduled communications, measured cost and time) that builds a greenfield web app; the code in this repo is the machine that carries that team. The plan was re-checked against this concept on 2026-11-19: question and decision protocol moved to Stage 1 (WP-141), and packages were added for delivery metrics (WP-132), milestone review and retro (WP-217), QA authoring (WP-315) and the Phase 0 playbook (WP-321). `artifact-map.yaml` assigns every artifact to a builder.

## Decisions made on 2026-11-19 (see `09-owner-decisions.md`)

The owner steers by commands, answers only critical-blocker questions and reviews results; agents collaborate without asking permission. Tech-lead approves ADRs; baseline freezes on approval; `/arima:run` covers Phase 4 and operations only; hosting is local Docker Compose with GitHub Actions CI (reference stack in ADR-0007); no role holds a GitHub token (the host posts comments, pushes, merges, tags); no AI attribution in any commit or PR. All open questions in the agent cards and feature specs are resolved under these principles.

WP-110 is done: `src/worktree.ts` (`createWorktree`, `removeWorktree`, `listWorktrees`, `pruneWorktrees`, `branchFor`, `slugify`) and `arima-worktree create|remove|list|prune` (exit 0/1/2, host only, in no role list). Worktrees live in `../<repo>-wt/<branch>` with a registry file `registry.json` there (run id, creating pid; kept outside `.arima/` so it never reaches the state branch). Create refuses protected, odd or existing branches and existing paths, checks the tree is clean at the base commit, and supports a sparse checkout from a plain path list (QA gets `tests/`, `api/`, `package.json`, no `src/` or `docs/`). Remove kills given process trees, retries with backoff, falls back to deleting the folder, prunes, and keeps the branch unless asked. `pruneWorktrees` (for dispatcher start) removes worktrees whose creating process is dead and keeps the branch (unpublished commits). QA needs its own branch (`qa/<item>-...`) because git allows one worktree per branch. Verified on Windows; the Linux run is the CI matrix's job (not run here). WP-190 (Docker) will use a local clone instead.

WP-141 is done: `src/questions.ts`. `raiseQuestions` turns a validated report's `questions[]` into: a **consult** if `addressed_to` is a role (recorded, routed with `pendingConsults`/`answerConsult`, never shown to the owner, blocks nothing); otherwise an owner question with a `Q` id and a Questions row; **blocking** ones move a story to Blocked through the state machine (actor `engine`, reason `Q-n: ...`); **non-blocking under `assume_and_log`** (the default policy) get a DEC row with a veto box and event `decision.made`; under `block_story` every question blocks. **Hard-stop matters are never assumed**: a `hard_stop` id from the agent or `engineHardStop` from an engine detector forces blocking and removes the default (tested for all 16 ids; a mutation was caught). `applyAnswers` marks a question answered when its `Answer` appears in the mirror, sets Status Answered, emits `question.answered`, and unblocks the story when no other blocking question of it is open (`budgetAvailable` can hold it). `expireQuestions` (RD-F04-6): a blocking non-hard-stop question takes its default with a DEC and unblocks; a hard stop stays blocked and is escalated once (`hardstop.hit` with `escalated: true`); a non-blocking one is flagged. `digestQuestions` returns at most 10, blocking first, then hard stops, then oldest, grouped by topic, with a count of the rest; `decisionsToVeto` lists DECs without a veto for the digest. Engine state is in `.arima/state/questions.json`. Question and DEC rows are engine entries named `st-<run>-...`, so the dispatcher must push with `{ idPrefix: 'st-' }`. `enqueueReportRecords` no longer enqueues questions; the dispatcher must call `raiseQuestions` for them (passing `placeholders` from `enqueueReportRecords` so a question can mention a `NEW-n`). Only stories are moved to Blocked; a question about a bug or other item is recorded and asked but blocks no story. The consult unit itself (planning a run for the addressed role) is WP-120/WP-109 work. **Live check, 2026-11-19, dev Notion workspace:** one non-blocking and one hard-stop question were raised through `raiseQuestions`; `arima-notion push` applied 3 rows (2 Questions, 1 Decision), the hard-stop row came back Blocking with an empty Default and the `[hard stop: new_paid_service]` prefix, the other kept Default Stripe with DEC-0001 (Chosen Stripe, Veto off) offered for veto; both question rows were then retired (Withdrawn). Left in the dev workspace: DEC-0001 (no retire status for decisions) and two Withdrawn Questions rows whose ids Q-001 and Q-002 came from a scratch counter, so the dev workspace may later reuse those ids.

WP-132 is done: `src/metrics.ts` (`itemTimes`, `gateWaitMs`, `agentVersusWall`, `dora`, `delivery`, `describeDelivery`), shown by `arima-cost` (a "Delivery" section and `delivery` in `--json`; the digest, WP-130, will use `describeDelivery`). Definitions are the spec's: lead = id issued to Released; cycle = first In Progress to first Done; touch = sum of the item's run durations; queue = every stay in Ready; human wait = PO Acceptance plus Blocked stays whose reason starts with a Q id, plus gate wait (`gate.opened` to `gate.decided`); flow efficiency = touch / lead; agent time vs wall time = summed durations vs the merged span of the runs. Also cost per accepted story (rework included), budget burn against the project cap, human minutes from the bills file, rework share, first-pass QA and estimate accuracy (those three in `cost.ts`). **`allocateId` now emits `id.issued`** with the item id: that is when an item is created. Items without that event start at their first status event. **DORA is "not yet measurable"** until a `deploy.production` event exists; WP-402/WP-403 must emit it with `data: { version, ok, hotfix?, items? }`, plus `deploy.rollback` (`data.version`), `merge.done` (item) and `incident.opened` (`data.version`) / `incident.closed` (item) for the failure, recovery and lead-time measures. Each measure has a definition test on a fixed fixture; a mutation of the human-wait rule was caught. Not done: the gate events `gate.opened` are not emitted anywhere yet (WP-330), so gate wait is 0 until then.

## Known traps

See `00-handoff.md` section 4 (backslashes in shell-generated code, scratch in `tmp/`, one-process token loading, run cost floor).
